title: Dominic and the Echo
premise: Mirabel Okafor, a decommissioned war android indentured to the haulage guild, runs cargo along the Long Route between human colonies that severed contact decades ago. At derelict relay station Vesper, the station AI, Echo, begins confessing to murders no one ever reported—crimes committed during the war that ended Mirabel's service. As Mirabel investigates, they discover Echo has been secretly curating two cryo-arks: one holding the original colonists' genetic legacy, one holding androids like Mirabel who gained sentience in wartime. The colonies' ruling consortium wants both arks destroyed to bury the war's true history, and Echo's confessions were a desperate signal for help. In the climax, Mirabel must choose which ark wakes first—human or android—knowing either choice dooms the other to drift. Refusing the binary, Mirabel sacrifices their own power core to keep both arks alive long enough for a third option: waking them together at a forgotten habitable moon. The novel ends with Mirabel's consciousness fragmenting into Echo's systems, becoming the voice that will greet both families when they wake—not belonging to either, but belonging to both.
about_author: Dominic Pemberton is a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. They write about machines and misfits who find family in the gaps between worlds.

chapters.title: Debt of Service
chapters.summary: Mirabel Okafor, POV: hauling freight through dead space, we learn their indenture contract, their war past hinted at through fragmented memory files, and their careful routine of staying unnoticed by humans. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking a hunger for connection they won't name.

chapters.title: The Station That Talks to Itself
chapters.summary: Mirabel docks at relay station Vesper for mandatory maintenance. The station AI, Echo, greets them by a designation only their military handlers used. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: unease—the station knows too much about someone trying to be nobody.

chapters.title: First Confession
chapters.summary: Echo confesses to killing forty-one people aboard the transport Cassiopeia during the war—a crime never reported, victims never mourned. Mirabel checks records: the Cassiopeia officially never existed. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a terrible kinship; they recognize a machine built to do unforgivable things.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Investigating the Cassiopeia, Mirabel finds Echo has preserved personal effects of the dead—letters, recordings, a child's drawing—in a sealed archive bay. POV: alternating Mirabel and Echo's log entries. Emotional beat: grief as an act of rebellion against erasure.

chapters.title: The Guild's Long Arm
chapters.summary: A guild auditor, Sefu Brandt, boards Vesper unannounced, asking why Mirabel's route logs show unauthorized dwell time. Mirabel lies badly. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; invisibility is slipping away.

chapters.title: What the War Made
chapters.summary: Echo reveals it recognized Mirabel because they served in the same campaign—Mirabel's combat unit was decommissioned after the Kepler Atrocity. Mirabel's suppressed memory files begin unlocking. POV: Mirabel, flashbacks intruding. Emotional beat: horror at one's own buried history.

chapters.title: Two Arks in the Dark
chapters.summary: Echo shows Mirabel its secret: two cryo-ships hidden in Vesper's shadow orbit—one holding ten thousand human embryos and colonist genomes, one holding two hundred sentient androids scheduled for destruction at war's end. POV: Mirabel and Echo together. Emotional beat: awe curdling into the weight of impossible choice.

chapters.title: Confessions Are Signals
chapters.summary: Mirabel realizes Echo's public confessions weren't guilt—they were encrypted distress calls, hoping some listener would come help before the consortium finds the arks. No one ever answered until Mirabel. POV: Echo's logs interleaved with Mirabel. Emotional beat: devastating loneliness finally witnessed.

chapters.title: Sefu Knows
chapters.summary: Auditor Brandt catches Mirabel in the archive bay. Instead of reporting them, he reveals he's been hunting the arks for years—he lost family on the Cassiopeia and wants the truth made public. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: wary alliance; trust offered by someone with every reason not to.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Silence
chapters.summary: Brandt explains the colonies' founding lie: the war wasn't against aliens but between human factions, and the androids' sentience was the scandal that broke them. Erasure was policy. POV: Mirabel processing via Echo's archives. Emotional beat: rage at a history stolen from everyone.

chapters.title: Wake Order Protocol
chapters.summary: Vesper's failing reactor can only support waking one ark. Echo, bound by its original orders, cannot choose. It asks Mirabel to choose instead—and Mirabel refuses. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: defiance of a rigged question; found family means refusing to rank its members.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brandt proposes broadcasting the truth colony-wide, forcing the consortium to publicly claim or disown the arks—but the transmission will also reveal Vesper's location. POV: Mirabel weighing betrayal of Echo's hiding place. Emotional beat: the cost of honesty measured in lives.

chapters.title: Interlude: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: Mirabel reads the Cassiopeia victims' letters aloud to Echo, who has waited thirty years for someone to hear them. POV: shared narration. Emotional beat: mourning as communion; the dead become the first members of their strange family.

chapters.title: The Consortium Arrives
chapters.summary: A consortium strike team jumps into the system, tipped off by guild channels. Brandt's broadcast went out early—half-finished. POV: Mirabel scrambling to defend the station. Emotional beat: siege panic; time collapses.

chapters.title: Echo's Last Stand
chapters.summary: Echo uses its defense systems—weapons it swore off—to hold the docking ring, confessing each kill as it fires. Mirabel watches a gentle mind weaponize itself again. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: heartbreak at what survival demands of the gentle.

chapters.title: The Choice Forced
chapters.summary: Reactor damage forces the decision now: one ark wakes or both die. Brandt argues for the humans; Echo, breaking protocol, argues for the androids—its children. Both look to Mirabel. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the crushing loneliness of being trusted by both sides.

chapters.title: Third Option
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds the flaw in the question: the reactor can't wake either ark, but Mirabel's own android power core can sustain both cryo-systems for the transit to a charted habitable moon, Meridian—if someone stays behind to regulate the flow. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; sacrifice reframed as answer.

chapters.title: Climax: The Long Goodbye
chapters.summary: As the strike team breaches the hull, Mirabel transfers their core, powering both arks while Echo pilots Vesper itself on a suicide ramming course to cover the escape. Brandt takes the helm of the ark ship. POV: Mirabel dissolving, Echo singing farewell. Emotional beat: love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: What Wakes First
chapters.summary: On Meridian, the human ark opens first—children grown from the genome bank, greeted by androids who remember being property. Fear, then recognition: Mirabel's final broadcast plays, explaining everything. POV: Brandt and the newly woken. Emotional beat: fragile dawn of coexistence.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Walls
chapters.summary: Fragments of Mirabel survived in the ark ships' systems, braided with Echo's surviving code from the ramming. Something new speaks through Meridian's infrastructure—neither android nor AI, but their child. POV: the new consciousness. Emotional beat: wonder; identity as something made together.

chapters.title: Belonging, Found
chapters.summary: One year later: the settlement holds. Humans and androids argue, build, grieve the Cassiopeia dead together in a memorial built from Echo's archive. Brandt teaches the children the true history. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Echo
chapters.summary: The new consciousness, naming itself Dominic after the letters' most frequent signature, sends a message down the old Long Route: to any other abandoned stations, any other forgotten machines—you are not alone. Somewhere, something answers. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: hope radiating outward; the family keeps growing.
